Date : 16/06/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal has been preferred by the appellant - original claimant against the respondents-original opponents under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short the Act) being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the judgment and award passed by the MACT (Aux), Vadodara in MACP No.719 of Shravansinh Devsinh Chauhan vs Laxmansinh Chatursinh Rajput on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57355895/

sentences.text:
Brief facts as emerging from the record are as under:
2.1
That on 13/12/2003, the appellant was travelling in bus bearing Registration No.RJ-36P 0292 which belonged to respondent No.2 and was travelling from his Village to Vadodara alongwith his relative.

That on 14/12/2003, in the morning when the bus reached near Bhaniyara Village, respondent No.1 was driving the bus in full speed rashly and negligently and dashed with a stationary crane and the appellant and other passengers seated in the bus suffered serious injuries. That the appellant was taken to Civil Hospital, Vadodara as he had sustained injuries on his left leg and two teeth were broken.
The offence was registered at Vaghodiya Police Station being I-CR No.174 of 2003.
The respondent No.1 was the driver of the truck and the respondent No.2 was the owner of the truck.

3. The claimant filed the claim petition against the driver and the owner and notices were duly served upon them and the respondents appeared before the learned tribunal and filed their written statement at Exh.14 and Exh.11 respectively.
Both the respondents specifically denied all the contents of the claim petition.

4. The learned tribunal after taking the evidence on record held both the opponents jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the appellant as the respondent No.1 was negligent while driving the bus involved in the accident and as the appellant was 13 years old and a minor on the date of the C/FA/2845/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 accident and he did not have any income considered the notional income of Rs.30,000/- per annum and applied multiplier of 15 and the medical bills of Rs.6,400/- which were produced by the appellant and awarded an amount of Rs.15,000/- towards the pain shock and suffering; Rs.7,500/-
as attendants, transportation and special diet and in all awarded amount of Rs.1,18,900/- under all heads with interest at the rate of 9% from the date of the petition till realization.
5. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the aforesaid award, the appellant-original claimant has approached this Court by way of this appeal.

6. I have heard learned Advocate Mr.Hiren Modi for the appellant and learned Advocate Mr.Paresh Darji for respondent no.2.
7.

It is mainly contended by the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant that the learned tribunal has grossly erred in calculating the income of the appellant at Rs.15,000/- per annum; that the learned tribunal has failed to consider that the appellant has disability of 46% and learned tribunal has not considered the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in the case of Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited & Anr. [AIR 2014 SC 736]; that Shravansinh Devsinh Chauhan vs Laxmansinh Chatursinh Rajput on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57355895/
2

sentences.text: in fact the parties had agreed to the disability of the appellant at the rate of 20% and as per the ratio laid down in Master Mallikarjun (supra), the appellant is entitled to an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- under all head and the medical charges.

Hence, the claim amount be enhanced and the respondent be ordered to C/FA/2845/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 pay the enhanced amount with interest.
8.

Learned Advocate for the respondent No.2 has submitted that the award of the learned Tribunal is just and proper and no interference is called for and hence the appeal of the appellant may be dismissed with costs.
9. I have gone through the R & P of the present appeal.

There is no dispute with regard to the occurrence of the accident and the fact that the appellant-original claimant was travelling in bus No.RJ-26P-0292 and travelling from his Village to Vadodara and the bus was being driven by respondent No.1 and the bus met with an accident on 14/12/2003 in the morning hours and the claimant sustained serious injuries.

It is also not in dispute that the bus dashed against a stationary crane and the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the respondent No.1.
10.

As far as the amount of compensation is concerned, the learned tribunal has considered the income of the appellant - original claimant who was a minor at the time of the accident to be of Rs.30,000/- per annum and the parties have agreed to consider the disability of 20% body as a whole

hence, the learned tribunal has awarded the multiplier of 15 and awarded an amount of Rs.90,000/- as future loss of income.
11.

In Master Mallikarjun's (supra) , the Hon'ble Apex Court while considering the claim of victim child has laid down the observations in para 8, which reads as under:-
"8. The age of the child and deformities on his body resulting in C/FA/2845/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 disability, have not been duly taken note of.

As held by this Court in R.D. Hattangadi vs. M/s. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. and Others[1], while assessing the non-pecuniary damages, the damages for mental and physical shock, pain and suffering already suffered and that are likely to be suffered,
any future damages for the loss of amenities in life like difficulty in running,
participation in active sports, etc., damages on account of inconvenience, hardship,
discomfort, disappointment, frustration, etc., have to be addressed especially in the case of a child victim.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi vs. M/s. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd. and Others[1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For a child, the best part of his life is yet to come.
While considering the claim by a victim child, it would be unfair and improper to follow the structured formula as per the Second Schedule to the Motor Vehicles Act for reasons more than one.
The main stress in the formula is on pecuniary damages.
For children there is no income.
The only indication in the Second Schedule for non- earning persons is to take the notional income as Rs.15,000/- per year.
A child cannot be equated to such a nonearning person.

Therefore, the compensation is to be worked out under the non- pecuniary heads in addition to the actual amounts incurred for Shravansinh Devsinh Chauhan vs Laxmansinh Chatursinh Rajput on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57355895/
3

entities.text: Shravansinh Devsinh Chauhan vs Laxmansinh Chatursinh Rajput
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: treatment done and/or to be done, transportation, assistance of attendant, etc.

The main elements of damage in the case of child victims are the pain, shock, frustration,
deprivation of ordinary pleasures and enjoyment associated with healthy and mobile limbs.
The compensation awarded should enable the child to acquire something or to develop a lifestyle which will offset to some extent the inconvenience or discomfort arising out of the disability.
Appropriate compensation for disability should take care of all the non-pecuniary damages.

In other words, apart from this head, there shall only be the claim for the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, transportation,
C/FA/2845/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 etc."
12.

While considering the case of the child observing that the child should appropriately be compensated for the disability, the Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down the yardstick for considering the disability to be compensated, which has been made in para 12 as under:-
"12.

Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; upto 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs.
For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Re.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
In the instant case, the disability is to the tune of 18%.
Appellant had a longer period of hospitalization for about two months causing also inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents.

The appellant, hence, would be entitled to get the compensation as follows: -
Head Compensation Compensation Amount Pain  Rs.3,00,000/-
and suffering already Rs.3,00,000/-undergone and  C/FA/2845/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship,
inconvenience, and discomforts, etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability Shravansinh Devsinh Chauhan vs Laxmansinh Chatursinh Rajput on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57355895/
4

Discomfort, inconvenience and  Rs.25,000/-
loss Rs.25,000/- of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization Medical and incidental  Rs.25,000/-
expenses Rs.25,000/- during the period of hospitalization for 58 days Future medical expenses for  Rs.25,000/-
Rs.25,000/- correction of the mal union of fracture and incidental expenses for such treatment Total Rs.3,75,000/-
13.

In the present case, the learned tribunal has with the consent of the parties considered the disability of 20% of the claimant who was a minor at the time of accident and in accordance with the observations made in Master Mallikarjun (supra), when the claimant has disability of above 10% and upto 30% body as a whole, the minor claimant would be entitled to an amount of Rs.3.00 Lakh.

14. Considering the age of the minor and the facts of the disability sustained in the vehicular accident, it would be appropriate that the yardstick which has been laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Mallikarjun (Supra) is followed in this matter.
Thus, accordingly, considering 20% disability for the C/FA/2845/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 16/06/2023 body as a whole of the minor victim, Rs.3,00,000/- is required to be granted.
15. The medical expense has been granted as Rs.6,400/-.
No dispute has been raised by the claimant.
Hence, the claimant would be entitled to total amount of Rs.3,06,400/-.

16. As the learned Tribunal has granted compensation of Rs.1,18,900/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum, the appellant-claimant would be entitled to additional amount of compensation of Rs.1,87,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the additional amount with interest at the rate of 6% per annum within eight weeks from the date of receipt of writ of this Court.

As the original claim petition is of the year 2004, the learned tribunal is directed to disburse the said enhanced amount to the claimants in the ratio apportioned by the tribunal to the claimants by NEFT/RTGS after due verification.
